# ghost_release (Resource)

Manages a release in a Ghost repository, and creates its tag when the tag doesn't exist yet.

Ghost creates the tag as soon as the release is created, **even for a draft**, so a draft's tag (though not the draft itself) is visible to anyone who can read the repository. Deleting the release keeps the tag. Ghost has no API for deleting tags: delete one with `git push origin --delete <tag>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ghost_repository" "example" {
  name      = "example"
  auto_init = true
}

# A published release. Ghost creates the v1.0.0 tag at the default branch
# unless it already exists.
resource "ghost_release" "v1" {
  repository = ghost_repository.example.full_name
  tag_name   = "v1.0.0"
  name       = "v1.0.0"
  body       = <<-EOT
    ## Changes

    * First stable release.
  EOT

  # Replacing the repository deletes its releases; this recreates the release
  # in the same apply. repo_id doesn't change when the repository is renamed.
  lifecycle {
    replace_triggered_by = [ghost_repository.example.repo_id]
  }
}

# A draft prerelease, tagged at a branch. Ghost creates the tag straight away,
# even for a draft, so the tag is visible before the release is published.
resource "ghost_release" "next" {
  repository       = ghost_repository.example.full_name
  tag_name         = "v1.1.0-rc.1"
  target_commitish = "main"
  draft            = true
  prerelease       = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `repository` (String) The repository's full name, `owner/slug`, e.g. `ghost_repository.example.full_name`. Renaming the repository updates this in place; pointing it at a different repository forces a new release. Replacing the repository deletes its releases, so add `lifecycle { replace_triggered_by = [ghost_repository.example.repo_id] }` to recreate the release in the same apply.
- `tag_name` (String) The tag, without the `refs/tags/` prefix, up to 250 characters. Tag names are case-sensitive. An existing tag is used as it is; otherwise Ghost creates it at `target_commitish`. Ghost can't move a release to another tag, so changing this forces a new release (the old tag is kept).

### Optional

- `body` (String) The release notes, in Markdown, up to 100,000 characters. Ghost can't generate release notes.
- `draft` (Boolean) Whether the release is an unpublished draft, visible only to people who can write to the repository. Defaults to `false`. Publishing a draft sets `published_at`; turning a release back into a draft keeps it.
- `name` (String) The release title, up to 200 characters. Without one, Ghost shows the tag name.
- `prerelease` (Boolean) Whether the release is marked as a prerelease. Defaults to `false`. The latest release is the newest published release that isn't a prerelease.
- `target_commitish` (String) The branch, tag or commit SHA to create the tag at when it doesn't exist yet. Defaults to the default branch. It is only used when the release is created: Ghost ignores it for an existing tag, and doesn't store it, so it is kept as configured, and changing it later only updates state (the tag doesn't move). It is null after import. `commit_sha` is the commit the tag points at.

### Read-Only

- `commit_sha` (String) The commit the tag points at. It follows the tag if it's moved, and is null once the tag has been deleted.
- `created_at` (String) When the release was created.
- `html_url` (String) The release's page in the web UI.
- `id` (String) The repository's full name and the numeric release ID, `owner/slug:release_id`.
- `node_id` (String) The GraphQL node ID.
- `published_at` (String) When the release was first published; null for a draft that has never been published.
- `release_id` (Number) The numeric release ID.
- `repository_id` (Number) The numeric ID of `repository`.
- `tarball_url` (String) The API URL of the tag's source tarball.
- `upload_url` (String) The URI template for uploading assets, taking `name` and `label`.
- `url` (String) The release's API URL.
- `zipball_url` (String) The API URL of the tag's source zip archive.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Releases are imported by the repository's full name and the numeric release
# ID, "owner/slug:release_id". target_commitish is null after import.
terraform import ghost_release.v1 my-user/example:123
```
